questions.q: In the pipeline from this lesson, what is the role of `transforms.Compose([transforms.ToTensor(), transforms.Normalize(...)])`?
options: It trains the model on a subset of the data
It chains together steps that convert raw images into normalized tensors, applied before batching
It defines the model architecture
It replaces the need for a DataLoader
questions.explain: transforms.Compose chains multiple preprocessing steps (here, converting to a tensor and normalizing) into a single callable applied to each image as it's loaded, before batching.

questions.q: Which components from earlier chapters does this lesson's training loop combine on top of the basic forward/backward/step pattern?
options: Gradient clipping and a learning rate scheduler step
A brand-new optimizer not covered anywhere else in the course
A completely different loss function unrelated to classification
Nothing — the loop is identical to the very first training loop in Chapter 1
questions.explain: The end-to-end loop layers gradient clipping (clip_grad_norm_) and a scheduler.step() call on top of the basic zero_grad/forward/backward/optimizer.step pattern introduced earlier in the course.

questions.q: Why does the inference code call both `model.eval()` and wrap the forward pass in `torch.no_grad()`?
options: model.eval() speeds up data loading, and no_grad() changes the loss function
model.eval() switches dropout/batch norm to inference behavior, and no_grad() skips building a computation graph since no backward pass is needed
Both calls are redundant and only one is actually necessary
no_grad() is required to enable gradient clipping
questions.explain: model.eval() changes the behavior of mode-dependent layers like dropout and batch norm, while torch.no_grad() avoids the memory and compute cost of tracking gradients when no backward pass will be run.

questions.q: Why is `image.unsqueeze(0)` needed before passing a single image through the model for inference?
options: To normalize the pixel values
To add a batch dimension of size 1, since the model expects a (batch, channels, height, width) shaped input
To convert the image from color to grayscale
To apply gradient clipping to the image
questions.explain: Models built with layers like Conv2d expect a batch dimension. A single loaded image lacks that dimension, so unsqueeze(0) inserts it, producing shape (1, C, H, W).

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is actually new about the end-to-end image classification pipeline compared to what earlier chapters already covered?
options: Every individual component (transforms aside, which build on Dataset/DataLoader concepts) is new and introduced for the first time here
Almost nothing is new in isolation — the pipeline assembles components (Dataset/DataLoader, the CNN, AdamW, CosineAnnealingLR, gradient clipping) that were each taught in earlier lessons
The pipeline replaces nn.Module entirely with a new API
The pipeline cannot use any of the CNN architecture from Lesson 24
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames this as an assembly exercise: the model, loss, optimizer, scheduler, and training-loop techniques were all introduced individually in earlier lessons, and this lesson's contribution is wiring them into one working pipeline.
